items.title: Vienna Plans New Heat System
items.gist: A familiar power-station landmark is coming down as the site shifts toward renewable heat.
items.summary: Vienna Energy plans to remove the tall chimney at the Donaustadt power station. The chimney will be taken apart in stages, not blown up. The site is set to gain geothermal energy, heat pumps and heat storage. City officials say the future system could supply 280,000 Vienna households. The project is part of a wider change to how the city produces heat.
items.host_open: Vienna is changing its skyline for a new source of heat. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Home Workers May Get Internet Costs
items.gist: Austria’s top court says employers must cover the work-related cost of home internet.
items.summary: Austria’s Supreme Court has ruled that employers must provide or pay for internet needed for regular remote work. The case began after a company policy offered laptops but excluded other costs. The court said an internet connection can count as a digital work tool. The amount owed may depend on the work-related share of the bill. Labour experts say employers should review their home-office agreements, while businesses have raised concerns about costs and tax rules.
items.host_open: Your home internet may now have a work-related price tag. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Ukraine War Reaches Libya
items.gist: A Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian ship in Libya has reportedly killed two Libyan naval officers.
items.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Libya, according to reports. The attack opened a new setting for the war, far from Ukraine’s front lines. The Libyan officers’ deaths were reported after the strike. Ukraine has described its attack as a military success. Libya’s internationally recognised government said neither side has the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its waters.
items.host_open: This conflict has reached far beyond its main front. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Gaza Strike Kills Hamas Official
items.gist: Gaza officials say an Israeli strike killed a senior Hamas security figure and members of his family.
items.summary: A strike hit the Shati refugee camp in Gaza City on November 25, according to Gaza civil defence. It said the attack killed Colonel Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, a senior figure in Hamas’s internal security service. His wife and two daughters were also reported killed. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas member. The reported deaths come amid continuing violence despite a ceasefire agreement reached in 2025.
items.host_open: Families have again been caught in the violence in Gaza. How does this news make you feel?

items.title: Eurostar Trains Face Strike Disruption
items.gist: An unexpected strike is disrupting trains through the Channel Tunnel in both directions.
items.summary: Eurostar says an unexpected strike is affecting train services between France and Britain. The disruption is hitting journeys in both directions through the Channel Tunnel. The company has not given detailed information about the strike. Reports say pay negotiations are under way. Travellers are being urged to check their journeys as talks continue.
items.host_open: A tunnel can be open and still leave travellers stuck. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Judge Rejects Ban on Partisan Ads
items.gist: A US judge declined to extend a block on government ads that critics called political propaganda.
items.summary: A federal judge in the United States declined to extend a temporary ban on taxpayer-funded government advertisements. Critics said the ads promoted partisan messages and President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections. The judge noted that the elections had already taken place. Democrats argued the ads could still harm their party during December runoffs and the 2028 election cycle. The decision leaves the ads unblocked for now.
items.host_open: The campaign season may be over, but the argument over ads is not. Did that surprise you?

items.title: A1 Plans 430 Net Job Cuts
items.gist: Austria’s largest telecom company plans to reduce its workforce while investing in newer technologies.
items.summary: A1 Austria plans a net reduction of 430 jobs in 2027. The plan involves 500 departures and 70 new hires in areas such as cloud services and cybersecurity. The company says it wants to cut costs by €300 million by 2030. It says some roles are linked to older technologies that are shrinking or have been switched off. A1 also says it will continue investing in networks and new technology.
items.host_open: A1 is cutting some roles while hiring for newer fields. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Thanksgiving Parade Postponed by Storm
items.gist: For the first time, New York’s Macy’s parade has been moved because of dangerous weather.
items.summary: Organisers have postponed New York’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday. The decision was made because of severe weather forecasts. The parade was due to mark its 100th year. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said strong winds could break tree limbs and bring down power lines. Officials said rescheduling was the safer choice for spectators and participants.
items.host_open: Even the balloons need to wait for calmer weather. How does that look from Austria?
